speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: asked the Prime Minister (a) what is the current number and percentage of Singaporeans in senior management roles at non-retail banks; (b) how has the number and percentage of Singaporeans across the entire finance sector changed over the last 10 years; and (c) what is the monthly salary of the 25th percentile, median and 75th percentile of Singaporeans, permanent residents and foreigners respectively across the sector's workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore or MAS started compiling detailed manpower data in the sector in the last few years.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In 2019, for senior roles in retail banks' local functions, Singaporeans accounted for about 70%.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In non-retail banks, where there is a higher concentration of regional and global functions, the proportion is lower.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: But as I have explained, while the share remains stable, the absolute number of Singaporeans holding senior level positions has been growing at a healthy pace as the base has expanded.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Two thousand six hundred Singaporeans now hold such positions, 900 more than five years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: That means an increase of 50% by absolute numbers.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The Member has asked for a comparison of 25th, 50th and 75th percentile salaries of Singaporeans, PRs and foreigners in the financial services sector.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: However, such a breakdown would not be meaningful, as we are not comparing like for like.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: A foreigner at the 50th percentile of foreigner's wage level in the financial sector could be hired for a very different role, from a Singaporean at the 50th percentile of the Singaporean wage level.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Notwithstanding, let me try to address the Member's queries by taking a broader view of the data, while taking care of the interpretation.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Across the financial sector, the median wage band of Singaporeans – because we collect the data by wage bands – the median wage band of Singaporeans is $6,000 to $8,000 monthly wage.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: While that for PRs and foreigners, they are similar, at the band of $8,000 to $10,000.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In the senior level positions, about half of Singaporeans earn above $30,000 per month.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It is the same for foreigners, while almost two thirds of PRs in the senior positions do.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Both sets of data are as one would expect.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Financial institutions very often bring in higher earning foreigners to perform specialised, or regional and global roles, and our rules constrain the flow of those who come in at the lower level.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: One would also expect those with stronger profiles and track records in Singapore to become more successful in attaining PR status.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In other words, these data show outcomes which reflect the fact that we regulate the inflow of foreigners and apply selective criteria in granting PR from those who were previously foreign PMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: If there was no regulation to control the inflow of Employment Pass holders and no criteria and conditions for PRs based on their track records, these earning differentials will naturally narrow or disappear.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We should focus our minds instead on the essential issue, which is how we can provide the best opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: As I explained in my speech earlier this week, we do this by staying open to the expertise that we need to grow as a global financial centre, investing in Singaporeans’ capabilities at every level and by ensuring fair employment practices amongst financial institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: MAS has been building our local talent pipeline for the financial sector and grooming more Singaporeans to be leaders and specialists, including giving them international exposure.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Our local talent pool has been expanding and we will continue to collaborate and work with the industry to continue this effort.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In terms of the proportion of Singaporeans, I think it was 70% of the financial services workforce, 44% in senior roles and this has been relatively stable over the past years.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Would MAS or the Government have a specific level they have in mind?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In relation to that, I also understand from the Minister's speech that there is the Finance Associate Management Scheme to groom young undergraduates and Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: How about in terms of supporting the middle management across the various spectrum, to support them into these senior roles?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: He asked why is it that not more Singaporeans are moving up to senior position roles.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That was exactly what I was trying to explain that, indeed, more Singaporeans have been moving up.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The percentage has not been moving – maybe that is why the Member misunderstood.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In my reply just now, I should have mentioned, it is not just Singaporeans taking up these senior roles here.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That is the way that we grow the sector and when the sector grows, there will be more opportunities.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Singaporeans are holding our own and taking and seizing some of these opportunities.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, the Member's second question, how do we support middle management in moving up, is exactly what we need to do.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If we keep saying, "Let's just be a pond.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Shut ourselves out from the lagoon and the lagoon shuts itself out from the sea", then we will always be a small pond.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: You can develop your middle management to take up senior positions, but your market will be small.
